title.en: Statistics by Simulation: Variation, Estimation and Testing

tagline: Reason about variation, estimates and tests by simulating them, and report effect sizes with intervals, their limits and how each was checked
description: Participants approach inference by simulation before formulas. They draw repeated samples to see variation, build bootstrap intervals for means, medians, differences and slopes, run permutation tests, and report effect sizes with intervals rather than bare p-values. They find multiple-testing and forking-path problems in reported results. Each lab ends with a note on how the result was checked, and the capstone is an analysis brief on a public dataset, defended orally. Power analysis and study design follow in SPC-STA-201 and SPC-EXP-201.
audience: Beginners. Career changers and non-computing graduates closing bridging gaps before advanced study, and computing graduates refreshing the mathematics behind models; a placement test lets participants skip any course whose content they already command.
prerequisites: FND-MTH-103 Probability for Data and AI
Probability shown in the placement test is accepted in place of FND-MTH-103
Computes group summaries with a DataFrame library (FND-DAT-102 or the pre-work notebook)

outcomes.text: Distinguish population, sample, parameter, statistic and sampling distribution, and explain what a standard error measures, given repeated samples from a known synthetic population
outcomes.evidence: supervised AI-off test, at least 70% correct

outcomes.text: Explain what p-values and confidence intervals mean and identify misreadings of them, given ten statements from synthetic reports
outcomes.evidence: each statement classified and corrected, eight of ten correct

outcomes.text: Identify multiple-testing, forking-path and confounding problems in a reported analysis, given a one-page synthetic summary
outcomes.evidence: a written critique naming each problem and its effect

outcomes.text: Compute bootstrap intervals for means, medians, group differences and regression slopes, given public data with skewed variables
outcomes.evidence: a notebook whose intervals agree on rerun with a new seed

outcomes.text: Implement permutation tests and report each result as an effect size with an interval, given two public datasets and stated questions
outcomes.evidence: notebooks with test code, intervals and a plain-language reading

outcomes.text: Apply family-wise and false-discovery-rate corrections and measure by simulation how often uncorrected tests produce false findings, given twenty outcomes with no true effect
outcomes.evidence: a table of false-finding rates with and without correction

case_study.name: The bakery chain (fictional)
case_study.summary: An unnamed chain of 24 neighbourhood bakeries in one city, with branches coded BR01 to BR24 and product lines L01 to L20; the labs speak to its operations manager, quality lead, finance analyst and customer insight lead by role only. Its data (a month of baskets, a known quarter of 40,000 baskets, waste records, a randomised discount trial and a promotion dashboard) is synthetic, written with seed 104; weeks 5 and 6 add two public-domain datasets bundled with statsmodels, read at run time and never copied into the course.

format_note: Extended: 8 weeks part-time, one session and one lab a week, weekly graded problem sets and a capstone

capstone.summary: A two-page analysis brief on a public dataset with estimate, interval, test, effect size and limits, submitted with its notebook and defended in a ten-minute oral check
capstone.submission: A link to a public GitHub repository with the two-page brief, the notebook with its outputs, and the dataset's source and licence; then a ten-minute oral check in which the participant walks through the brief and reruns one test with a change the assessor specifies

rubric.criterion: Question, dataset, source and licence, unit and scope stated; groups under 30 rows suppressed
Estimate with a bootstrap interval resampled the way the data were collected; the interval agrees on rerun with a new seed
Test with its null model stated, a permutation test, the effect size with an interval and a plain-language reading
Limits: confounding, multiple comparisons and forking paths named where they apply, and what the analysis cannot show
Notebook reruns from top to bottom; a record of how each result, and any AI-assisted step, was checked
